title: RAW_UNREVIEWED speculative: local anaphors keep two products from one plant on separate downstream tracks
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_UNSELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Creative extension grounded in one complete Lonitzer Dipsacus entry: the wine-cooked root becomes a stored medicine referred to as 'quod medicamentum', while 'eadem aqua' continues the distinct water resting on the leaves and assigns it another use. Hypothesis: a whole account that mentions multiple products must preserve separate local antecedents even when both belong to one plant entry. This exact co-tracking constraint is speculative and is not asserted by the source as a general rule; no target words are assigned.

source_evidence.quote:
In vino cocta radix usque dum cerae crassitiem assumat, rimas fistulasque sedis illita sanat. Quod medicamentum in testaceo vase ad annuum tempus recondi potest: verrucas quoque pensiles curat.
Aqua foliis insidens oculorum caligini et rubedini medetur. Eadem aqua maculas faciei exterit.

design.distinctive_constraint: Preserve two distinct antecedent chains: cooked wine-root preparation → stored medicamentum; leaf-bearing water → eye/face uses.
design.falsifier: The proposed source-level bookkeeping fails if either anaphor cannot be assigned locally from this complete entry, or if the whole model needs arbitrary cross-links between the root preparation and leaf water.
